subject.title: feat(skills): declarative cron-trigger metadata in SKILL.md frontmatter

question: Should OpenClaw add a public SKILL.md automation metadata contract for scheduled/event-triggered skills, and if so should it live in top-level frontmatter, metadata.openclaw, or a plugin/ClawHub-owned manifest surface?
rationale: The source gap is real, but autonomous skill scheduling is a public product and security boundary; source inspection cannot choose the permission model, field placement, or whether existing bundled-plugin scheduler APIs are the intended extension seam.

options.title: Design a permissioned SKILL.md contract
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a maintainer-approved metadata, approval, revocation, audit, and scheduler registration design before implementation.

options.title: Route scheduling to plugins only
options.body: Use the existing bundled-plugin scheduled-turn and cron hook APIs as the supported path, and do not add schedule semantics to plain SKILL.md files.

options.title: Document triggers only
options.body: Accept only a non-executing documentation or indexing field until a security model for autonomous execution is approved.

recommendation.title: Design a permissioned SKILL.md contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a maintainer-approved metadata, approval, revocation, audit, and scheduler registration design before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses the skill, plugin, cron, and security boundary areas where the accessible history and VISION.md ownership signals point most clearly to steipete.
